title: p0114
universal_lens: Cortical dynamics are modeled as a continuous-time Markov process where phenomenological salience is inversely proportional to the eigenvalue decay rate of the local connectivity matrix. High-frequency currents rapidly dissipate, yielding low subjective intensity, while restricted topological bottlenecks induce prolonged excitation and heightened awareness.
gsi_mapping: In Bayesian inference, high-probability priors act as copious discharge channels, causing rapid belief updates with minimal epistemic friction. Unexpected data encounters topological bottlenecks, prolonging posterior variance and triggering high-confidence conformal alerts due to the slow dissipation of predictive error across the feature space.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning maps cortical regions to game-state nodes. Probable transitions (habitual plays) drain kinetic energy instantly, bypassing conscious tactical evaluation. Defensive breakdowns create topological bottlenecks, forcing prolonged state residence and intense cognitive focus on anomalous spatial configurations or unexpected opponent maneuvers.

primitives.name: Phenomenological Dwell Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: All consciousness seems to depend on a certain slowness of the process in the cortical cells.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: I: Intensity of consciousness (dimensionless), \lambda_{\text{min}}: Smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian connectivity matrix (s^{-1}), \phi: Cortical excitation potential (V), \mathbf{x}: Spatial coordinate in cortex (m).
primitives.assumptions: Cortical tissue behaves as a diffusive medium; consciousness scales linearly with the residence time of the excitation packet within a localized manifold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As \lambda_{\text{min}} \to \infty (infinitely fast diffusion/drainage), I \to 0, resulting in complete unconscious processing despite massive neural activity.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to the GSE dwell-time metric for player attention. A play executed at speeds exceeding cognitive diffusion limits becomes invisible to defensive tracking systems.
layer2.telemetry: Mean reaction latency (ms) vs. stimulus velocity.

primitives.name: Topological Bottleneck Amplifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: If B, on the contrary, has no such copious channel of discharge, the excitement will linger there longer ere it diffuses itself elsewhere, and our consciousness of the sort of object that B makes us feel will be strong.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \tau_B: Residence time in region B (s), \mathbf{K}_{B \to \neg B}: Transition rate matrix from B to external states (s^{-1}), P(t): Probability mass remaining in B (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Neural pathways form a directed graph where edge weights represent conductance; isolated subgraphs trap probability mass.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when \text{Tr}(\mathbf{K}_{B \to \neg B}) = 0, creating an absorbing state where excitation never decays (epileptic seizure or infinite attentional lock).

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI anomaly detection. When incoming telemetry fails to map to standard transition matrices, the system enters a high-residence diagnostic loop, amplifying alert severity.
layer2.telemetry: Conformal p-value persistence duration under streaming data.

primitives.name: Probabilistic Substitution Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: In other words, just in proportion as associations are habitual, will the qualities of the suggested thing tend to substitute themselves in consciousness for those of the thing immediately there; or, more briefly, just in proportion as an experience is probable will it tend to be directly felt.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \hat{S}_{\text{felt}}: Felt state representation (dimensionless embedding), \mathcal{T}: Associative transition kernel (dimensionless), \mathbb{P}: Prior probability distribution over states (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Perceptual reality is a weighted superposition of immediate sensory input and high-probability prior expectations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \mathbb{P}(s') \gg \mathcal{T}(s|s_{\text{obs}}), hallucination occurs; the model completely overrides physical observation with probabilistic priors.

layer2.mapping: Direct mapping to GSE predictive modeling. Defenses react to the highest probability offensive formation rather than the actual spatial configuration if the transition speed exceeds the dwell threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of false-positive tactical reads against actual play outcome.

The foundational operator here is the inverse relationship between current velocity and phenomenological intensity. Mathematically, we treat the cortex as a Riemannian manifold equipped with a diffusion tensor. The 'rapidity' of a current corresponds to the gradient magnitude of the excitation field \nabla \phi. If the geodesic paths between cortical regions A and B are highly conductive (low resistance edges in the adjacency matrix), the excitation undergoes rapid exponential decay, characterized by a large spectral gap in the Laplacian. This results in a vanishing integral of the squared norm of the excitation over time—meaning zero conscious registration.

Conversely, a 'topological bottleneck' implies a sparse connection or a high-resistance boundary condition. Here, the excitation packet reflects internally, increasing its dwell time \tau. The 'probabilistic substitution' emerges naturally from this framework: habitual associations correspond to pre-conditioned, low-resistance manifolds. When sensory input arrives, the system's prior expectation acts as a deep attractor basin. If the transition probability to this basin is sufficiently high, the excitation slides into the expected state before the raw sensory data can fully register. Thus, we do not perceive the raw data; we perceive the high-probability trajectory. In GSE terms, this explains why elite athletes often 'see' the play before it happens—they are riding the low-resistance probabilistic manifold, substituting the predicted state for the observed one. Failure modes occur when the real-world transition violates the high-probability manifold, creating a sudden bottleneck and a spike in conscious awareness (the 'surprise' factor).
